title: Coming and going
topic: הוֹלֵךְ, נוֹסֵעַ, בָּא, חוֹזֵר in the present
why: The four verbs of movement in the present, telling apart going on foot (הוֹלֵךְ) and going by vehicle (נוֹסֵעַ), with לְאָן and time words. You reuse the four present-tense forms from unit 5 and the prepositions from the previous lesson.

{"lessons": ["

Going: on foot or by vehicle?

In English, you just \"go\" everywhere. Hebrew first asks how: on foot, it's הוֹלֵךְ; by bus, train, or car, it's נוֹסֵעַ.

on foot (לָלֶכֶת)by vehicle (לִנְסֹעַ)
m. sg.הוֹלֵךְ holekhנוֹסֵעַ nose'a
f. sg.הוֹלֶכֶת holekhetנוֹסַעַת nosa'at
m. pl.הוֹלְכִים holkhimנוֹסְעִים nos'im
f. pl.הוֹלְכוֹת holkhotנוֹסְעוֹת nos'ot

These are the four forms you already know (כּוֹתֵב, כּוֹתֶבֶת…). The little dash (a) under the final ע of נוֹסֵעַ is read just before it: nose-a.

אֲנִי הוֹלֶכֶת לַשּׁוּק, וְהוּא נוֹסֵעַ לְחֵיפָה.I'm going to the market (on foot), and he's going to Haifa. [ani holekhet la-shuk, ve-hu nose'a le-Kheifa.]

The destination takes לְ: לַשּׁוּק, לְחֵיפָה, לִירוּשָׁלַיִם. The one very common exception: הַבַּיְתָה (habayta), \"home,\" with the direction ה you saw in יָמִינָה.

", "

Coming and coming back

to come (לָבוֹא)to come back, return (לַחֲזֹר)
m. sg.בָּא baחוֹזֵר khozer
f. sg.בָּאָה ba'aחוֹזֶרֶת khozeret
m. pl.בָּאִים ba'imחוֹזְרִים khozrim
f. pl.בָּאוֹת ba'otחוֹזְרוֹת khozrot
הִיא חוֹזֶרֶת הַבַּיְתָה מֵהָעֲבוֹדָה.She's coming home from work. [hi khozeret habayta me-ha-avoda.]

English gets by with \"where,\" adding \"to\" or \"from\" at the end of the sentence; Hebrew has three separate words: אֵיפֹה? (where are you?), לְאָן? (where are you going to?), מֵאֵיפֹה? (where are you from?).

לְאָן אַתָּה נוֹסֵעַ?Where are you going? (to a man) [le'an ata nose'a?]

The trap: using אֵיפֹה for a destination. If you're moving, it's לְאָן.

", "

Now, today, tomorrow

HebrewPronunciationMeaning
עַכְשָׁוakhshavnow
הַיּוֹםhayomtoday
מָחָרmakhartomorrow
בָּעֶרֶבba-erevin the evening, tonight

Good news: just like in English (\"tomorrow I'm leaving\"), the present is enough for a plan in the near future.

מָחָר אֲנַחְנוּ נוֹסְעִים לִירוּשָׁלַיִם בָּרַכֶּבֶת.Tomorrow we're going to Jerusalem by train. [makhar anakhnu nos'im lirushalayim ba-rakevet.]
עַכְשָׁו אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לָעֲבוֹדָה בָּרֶגֶל.Now I'm walking to work. [akhshav ani holekh la-avoda ba-regel.]

To say who with: עִם (with): אֲנִי בָּא עִם נֹעָה, I'm coming with Noa.
